questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether going to a sauna is good for your health
How to build a sauna at home
Why Finland has such cold winters
The dangers of swimming in the sea in winter
questions.why: They look at why people love saunas and whether there is medical evidence they're good for us.

questions.q: How do Georgie and Neil feel about saunas?
options: They both love them
They have never tried one
Georgie isn't a fan because it's too hot, but Neil likes them
Neil finds them uncomfortable, but Georgie loves them
questions.why: Georgie doesn't like being too hot, while Neil says he quite likes a sauna and feels refreshed.

questions.q: How does Georgie describe a typical sauna?
options: A large pool of hot water, usually outside
A small wooden room heated with steam to 80°C
A room kept at normal body temperature
An outdoor fire on the beach with benches
questions.why: She says a typical sauna is a small wooden room heated with steam to around 80°C.

questions.q: What do the people at the beach sauna in Wales say they enjoy about it?
options: Meeting new friends from the local area
Losing weight quickly before the summer
Getting warm before swimming in the cold sea
Relaxing, easing tense muscles and stress
questions.why: They say it's relaxing, great for tense muscles, and leaves them feeling completely reset.

questions.q: According to Professor Damian Bailey, what share of people in Finland use saunas?
options: About 40%
About half
About 90%
Almost nobody
questions.why: He says of five million people in Finland, 90% use saunas.

questions.q: What health benefit does Damian mention among sauna-goers in Finland?
options: A 40% lower risk of dying from any cause
They sleep about 40% longer each night
They have 90% fewer colds every winter
They lose around 20kg of weight a year
questions.why: He says there's a 40% reduction in all-cause mortality with the sauna-goers.

questions.q: Why does Damian say more research is still needed?
options: Because the Finnish studies were very small
Because saunas have become more dangerous
Because doctors don't agree on the results
The data comes from watching, not from trials
questions.why: He says it's observational data, so 'we really do need' randomised controlled trials.

questions.q: What does Damian suggest about the current evidence?
options: It should be ignored until proper trials are done
It isn't perfect, but it covers so many people
It clearly proves that saunas are dangerous
It only applies to people living in Finland
questions.why: He says it's based on thousands of sauna-goers, so 'we can't turn our noses up' at it.
